study_identification.title: Lifespan Normative Modeling of Brain Microstructure

study_characteristics.study_objective: Construct a large-scale normative model of white matter microstructure across the lifespan using diffusion MRI, derive centile trajectories by age and sex, and demonstrate clinical utility via anomaly detection and model adaptation in MCI, dementia, and 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: ROI-wise AUCs computed for classifying dementia/MCI vs controls across 10 repetitions; permutation tests (1,000 samples) to derive p-values; FDR correction per metric across ROIs; summarization of extreme deviation rates (|Z|>2) by group and ROI.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Large-scale HBR-based normative models of WM microstructure (N=54,583; age 4–91) yield lifespan centile curves and detect clinically meaningful deviations in MCI, dementia, and 22q11.2 deletion syndrome, with robust within-domain and cross-domain validation.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The models estimated ROI-wise trajectories for FA, MD, AD, RD across 21 JHU-WM regions and Global-WM, showing typical inverted-U (FA) and U-shaped (diffusivity) age curves. Validation used repeated 80/20 train–test splits (10×) with calibration diagnostics (SMSE, MSLL, Shapiro–Wilk, skewness, kurtosis). In anomaly detection, dementia showed highest AUCs in CGH for RD (0.74), MD (0.70) and FA (0.65), and in BCC for AD (0.67); MCI AUCs ranged 0.55–0.60 (e.g., SCC MD 0.60; BCC AD 0.67; FX FA/MD 0.58/0.59). Extreme deviations (|Z|>2) were predominantly positive for diffusivity and negative for FA (e.g., RD positive deviations: 37% CGH and 25% SCC in dementia; 17% SCC and 11% CGH in MCI). External model adaptation (NIMHANS: MCI/dementia; UCLA: 22qDel) demonstrated transferability.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: ENIGMA-DTI protocol not optimized for very early childhood (3–5 years); potential CSF partial volume contamination in certain regions (e.g., fornix); reliance on single-shell DTI limits microstructural specificity; more advanced distributional models (e.g., warping, SHASH, VAEs) and multi-shell metrics are suggested for future work.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Batch defined by dMRI protocol and handled via HBR partial pooling; age modeled with cubic B-splines (5 knots); sex used as grouping variable; model adaptation used PCNtoolkit 'transfer' to adapt hyperparameters to new sites (using 50% local HCs).

general_notes.general_notes: Training data pooled from 19 datasets spanning 37 distinct dMRI protocols; repeated 80/20 splits stratified by site; PCNtoolkit v29 (Python 3.9) used for HBR with NUTS sampling; ROI set per ENIGMA-DTI/JHU-WM (21 ROIs + Global-WM). Full dataset list and per-dataset demographics provided in Table 2; preprocessing details and dataset-specific pipelines listed, with DiPy/FSL/ANTs and ENIGMA-DTI protocol for ROI extraction.
